parts.text:
5
Which calculation produces a vector quantity?
A
current  time
B
final displacement – initial displacement
C
done
work
time
D
2
1  mass  (speed)2

hints: Look at the quantities named in each calculation: current, time, displacement, work done, mass and speed.
Recall that displacement is a vector with direction, while current, time, work done, mass and speed are all scalars.
Work out what physical quantity each calculation makes - charge, change in displacement, power, kinetic energy - and decide which one still needs a direction.
walkthrough: Identify the nature of each starting quantity: displacement is a vector, while current, time, work done, mass and speed are scalars.
Recall that a vector quantity has both magnitude and direction, so combining vectors can keep direction while combining only scalars cannot create direction.
Check option A: $Q = I \times t$ gives electric charge in coulombs, a scalar.
Check option C: $P = W/t$ gives power in watts, a scalar. Check option D: $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ gives kinetic energy in joules, a scalar.

Check the remaining calculation: change in position found from final displacement minus initial displacement has both magnitude in $\text{m}$ and direction, so it is a displacement and hence a vector.
Therefore the only calculation producing a vector is final displacement minus initial displacement. This is option B

A.explanation: Current $\times$ time gives charge $Q = It$, which has magnitude only and is a scalar.

B.explanation: Displacement is a vector, so final displacement minus initial displacement gives change in displacement, which still has magnitude and direction.

C.explanation: Work done divided by time gives power $P = W/t$, which has magnitude only and is a scalar.

D.explanation: $\frac{1}{2} \times$ mass $\times$ (speed)$^2$ gives kinetic energy, which has magnitude only and is a scalar.
